[Help: source alignment flags and evidence fractions](report-help.html#provenance){target="_blank"}

The **Source genomic alignments** column counts extracted query sequences by
the SAM status of the genomic alignment used to extract them: primary (neither
0x100 nor 0x800), secondary (0x100), supplementary (0x800), or both when both
flags are set. These are source-query counts across extraction channels, not
unique-read counts, independent alignments, allele frequencies or support for
each TE hit. One event can contain several statuses; the same read can contribute
through several alignments or channels. VCF-reported sequences have no single
source alignment (`not applicable`); INSIDER assembly calls are also not applicable.
`Unknown` means the metadata were not recorded. These statuses are not BLAST-hit
ranks, are not inferred from MAPQ, and do not change TE selection or frequencies.

## Ambiguous variable TE calls

Only reported INSIDER/OUTSIDER events with at least two distinct TE labels belong in this table. Sequence provenance distinguishes competing annotations on one query, hits on separate query regions, and evidence from different insertion sequences or reads. These are descriptions of raw alignment evidence, not confirmed alleles, components or SWAPs. Sequence differences can include read errors. VCF-reported alleles have no assigned read identity and may be consensus sequences.

Fraction is the candidate's evidence count divided by the sum of candidate counts
for that event, displayed as a percentage; it is not an allele frequency or a
share of unique reads. Queries / sequences / reads / VCF counts refer to the whole
candidate group: BLAST queries, distinct exact insertion sequences, known source
reads, and VCF-reported queries. Provenance indicates whether sequence origins
and insertion sequences are complete, partial, or unavailable. Raw HSPs
(High-scoring Segment Pairs) are the original local BLAST alignments.

# Execution times

Durations are measured wall times for individual workflow jobs. Jobs can run concurrently: their sum is **not** the elapsed time of the whole analysis. Measurements include reused results from earlier executions when a run resumes. Report preparation and rendering are excluded.

## Nearby-call candidates

This view exposes calls whose breakpoint anchors fall within the configured window. It is deliberately labelled **candidate proximity**, not a resolved biological locus: TE family is never used as locus identity, and proximity alone cannot prove alternative, nested or composite alleles.

## Interpretation boundary

This report visualizes the legacy-compatible `TE_INFOS.bed` table without changing its scientific values. Frequencies retain the compatibility algorithms of the migrated workflow. The resident catalog is a separate assembly annotation and must not be interpreted as an insertion polymorphism table. Nearby-call groups and resident copy relations are exploratory candidates only. Cohort-level multi-allelic inference must use the normalized locus model and explicit cross-sample evidence.
